target_customer: B2B sales teams wanting new target accounts similar to their existing customers
problem: Sales teams struggled to find new accounts to prospect. SalesSift used machine learning on the profile of existing customers to recommend new companies to target.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for lead lists and recommendations
product_category: Sales lead sourcing and lookalike account recommendation

founders.name: Chris Ashby
founders.background_notes: The YC page names only Chris Ashby and gives no biography.

competitors.name: Mattermark
competitors.what: Company database used to build lead and investor lists
competitors.traction_then: Over 60 customers using it for lead qualification per its own blog, undated

technical_complexity.rationale: Lookalike scoring needs company data coverage and a ranking model, which is standard machine learning work for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Recommendations depended on third party company data, and incumbents with larger datasets could offer the same feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found in sources. No acquisition of SalesSift was found.

market_need_then: B2B teams were adopting sales intelligence tools in 2014, shown by launches of data products like Mattermark, but no source states SalesSift customer demand.

branding.domain_note: Used salessift.com per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage found about the brand. Similar names such as Leadsift and Sift AI cause confusion in search.

outcome_analysis: SalesSift, formerly LeadFinch, was a two person lead sourcing startup in YC Summer 2014. Public sources give no raise beyond a small database entry and no shutdown date or cause, so the cause of failure is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 503 in this session, so it may be dead. The seed of 120000 at a 2.0m valuation rests on one database (Dealroom), whose description on that page appears to belong to another company, so treat it as unreliable. Mattermark source is dated about four months after the batch. The cause of shutdown is not public.
